agency: City of Palm Bay Mayor (via News 6)
text: Fairhaven area of Palm Bay is inaccessible because of flooding; no specific roads named.

agency: State of Florida, Governor's Office (via WFTV)
text: State of emergency declared for Brevard and six other counties (Executive Order 26-227) because of flooding. Effective immediately for 60 days; includes price-gouging protections.

agency: Brevard Public Schools (via Florida Today/Yahoo News)
text: Because of the extent of flooding across the county, all Brevard Public Schools campuses and district offices will stay closed Tuesday, Nov. 3. Schools are expected to reopen Wednesday.

agency: Brevard County Supervisor of Elections (via News 6)
text: Because of the historic flooding, some Election Day precinct polling locations are being moved temporarily for Tuesday's General Election. Voters should check where their precinct will vote before going.

agency: Brevard County Emergency Management (via Spectrum News 13)
text: Water on some roads has gone down since earlier in the day, but county officials still ask residents not to leave home unless they absolutely must or are under evacuation orders. The Red Cross has opened a shelter in Cocoa at Parker Memorial Missionary Baptist Church.

agency: Brevard County Sheriff's Office (via Space Coast Daily)
text: Sheriff Wayne Ivey says courts will be back in session Tuesday, Nov. 3, and many government offices are expected to reopen as flooding damage is assessed. Brevard Public Schools stay closed Tuesday so the district can inspect buildings. The full extent of flood damage is not yet known, so residents should stay off the roads unless they need to travel.

agency: Eastern Florida State College (via Space Coast Daily)
text: Eastern Florida State College stays closed Tuesday, Nov. 3, because of flooding.

The boil water notice now covers all West Melbourne water customers. It replaces the earlier notice, which covered only the area south of US 192 and east of Hollywood Blvd. The City of Melbourne, which supplies West Melbourne's water, reported a water main break whose exact location is not yet known. Boil all water for drinking, cooking, making ice, brushing teeth and washing dishes, or use bottled water, until the city says the water is safe.

A water main break in Melbourne's system has cut water pressure, and in some cases all water service, for customers in Indialantic, Indian Harbour Beach, Melbourne Beach, Satellite Beach and some unincorporated areas that get their water from the City of Melbourne.

agency: City of Cocoa Beach (via News 6 WKMG)
text: Too much water is flowing into the Cocoa Beach wastewater treatment plant and lift stations. Residents, especially in the south end and Snug Harbor, are asked to limit nonessential water use.

Several roads and intersections in West Melbourne are still closed by flooding as of 8 a.m. Tuesday. Drive slowly and carefully, especially near flooded neighborhoods, because wakes from passing vehicles can push water into homes. Officials are still checking whether flooded areas are safe to travel.
Several Melbourne roads are still fully closed because floodwater has not drained. Many abandoned vehicles are still blocking roads and slowing emergency response.
